title: Coefficient, product and scheme coherence of normalized continuous-set comparisons
statement:
Use compatible universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ range over schemes [def-pc-scheme] with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathcal T$ be the category of Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces and continuous maps. Put $\underline D(S)=C(S,D)$ on profinite spaces and $F_{D,X}(U)=C(|U|,D)$ [def-sfb-continuous-set-presheaf]. Suppose these are sheaves, and for every $X$ and $D\in\mathcal T$ a morphism $\sigma_{D,X}:p_X^*\underline D\to F_{D,X}$ is specified by the normalization that its adjunct sends $b:S\to D$ to $b r_{X,S}$ under the composite adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], with $r_{X,S}$ as in [lem-sfb-relative-profinite-test-labels]. No invertibility of $\sigma$ is assumed. Then $F_{h,X}\sigma_{D,X}=\sigma_{D',X}p_X^*\underline h$ for every continuous $h:D\to D'$. The maps $\sigma$ respect the canonical finite-product identifications for continuous-function sheaves and the finite-product comparisons for $p_X^*$, including the empty product (the one-point coefficient space). For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$, let $c_{f,D}:f^{-1}F_{D,X}\to F_{D,Y}$ be the adjunct, for the actual inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], of the map $\rho_{f,D}:F_{D,X}\to f_*F_{D,Y}$ given on $V\to X$ by $s\mapsto s\circ|V\times_XY\to V|$. If $\kappa_f:f^{-1}p_X^*\to p_Y^*$ is the specified point-pullback composition comparison, then
$$c_{f,D}\circ f^{-1}(\sigma_{D,X})=\sigma_{D,Y}\circ\kappa_{f,\underline D}.$$
The $c_{f,D}$ satisfy identity and composition: under the inverse-image identity comparison $c_{\mathrm{id},D}$ is the identity, and for $Z\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{f}X$, after identifying $(fg)^{-1}$ with $g^{-1}f^{-1}$ one has $c_{fg,D}=c_{g,D}\circ g^{-1}(c_{f,D})$.

proof.text: Transpose the coefficient square through the composite point adjunction. Naturality of its Hom equivalence changes postcomposition and precomposition into the two composites of adjuncts. Evaluate at every profinite S and b:S→D and apply the supplied normalization; associativity of continuous-map composition proves equality. Injectivity gives the square.

proof.text: Construct the product limit of the continuous-function presheaves directly: lift a cone by assigning to each section the continuous map whose i-th coordinate is its i-th component. Continuity is continuous_pi; naturality and uniqueness hold coordinatewise. Reflect the limit through the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves, for both profinite and scheme sites. The construction includes the empty family.

proof.text: Prove a generic transpose formula for a component of the inverse conjugation of a right-adjoint transformation, using unit_conjugateEquiv_symm and naturality. Apply it to the identity comparison. Its transpose is the inverse direct-image identity, whose section formula is exactly precomposition with the first projection in continuousSetDirectImageMap.

proof.text: Apply the generic conjugate transpose formula to the composition comparison. The composite Hom equivalence is the successive pair of Hom equivalences. Their naturality and the definition of continuousSetPullbackMap give the two successive rho maps followed by lowerStarComp. Evaluate on a test object U and section s. The equality pullbackComp_left_fst_fst proves that restriction along these three maps is restriction along the composite projection.

proof.text: For the normalized scheme square generalize the structure maps to kX:X→Spec Z and kY:Y→Spec Z with f≫kX=kY. Substitute the equality. Transpose through the composite of the point adjunction with the two scheme adjunctions. The left side becomes the normalized adjunct for X followed by rho. The generic conjugate transpose formula changes the inverse point compositor into lowerStarComp.inv on the right. Evaluate at S,b and apply the two normalization assumptions. The explicit definition of continuousSetRelativeTestProjection reduces equality to pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_hom_fst. Specialize the structure maps and use the component formula for profinitePointSetSchemeComp. No existence, uniqueness, or invertibility theorem for realization is used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-c96ec0ab2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged from live. The item is still unsplit in both live and side-live, so nothing supersedes it, and it has no repair note. Its six steps expand the old steps 7 and 8 of the parent realization node (the NV re-split, PASS) and drop none of their arguments. Steps 2-3: coefficient naturality is h(b r) = (h b) r. Finite products are checked coordinatewise through P_X(pr_i), with left-exactness from the point node, the base-change definition and the left-exact site theorem. The empty product is the terminal case. Steps 4-6: rho_f is natural by the fibre-product projection equations, and rho_fg = f_*(rho_g) rho_f. The main equation holds: transposing c_f f^{-1}(sigma_X) gives R_X(rho_f) alpha_X, whose value at (S,b) is b r_X |pr| = b r_Y by the label base-change clause. Transposing sigma_Y kappa_f through the composite adjunction and then delta gives alpha_Y by the conjugate unit equation. Composition and identity follow by successive transposes. Sigma is never inverted. Edge cases checked: empty X, S or D, one-point D, f = id, and two composable maps. Sources: HRS Ex. 3.1 p.6, and Stacks 0037, 0DV0, 0B65, 00WX and 00X6. No SGA is cited. I accept the declared tool uses of profinite-point-pullback and left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor (both sk-thm-properbasechange) as generic site tools. The other cited nodes outside the unit are Mathlib leaves. No duplicate: the sibling kan-evaluation node gives sigma's existence and values on contractible affines, not this coherence. FIX (C4): step 1 uses pi_{X*} but did not cite def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, which defines it; I added that node. Steps 5-6 need kappa_f and the compositor of (fg)^{-1} with g^{-1}f^{-1} to be the adjunction-compatible ones. The point node says only 'the inverse-image composition comparison'. lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor says the composition isomorphisms are the ones compatible with the adjunctions, so I added it to the uses of both steps and reworded them. proof_deps is unchanged.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
